configs.description: Dual 400W AC supplies (PSU-401-AISB, C14 inlet, intake airflow) with five FAN-402825-HD exhaust fans. The datasheet's AC input rating is 100 to 240 V at 6 A.
configs.name: ac

configs.description: The router as every figure draws it - two PSU-401-DISB 400W DC supplies in the front bays, five FAN-402825-HD exhaust fans at the rear, and the thirty traffic ports empty. No orderable chassis part number appears in any held document; see the chassis-sku gap.
configs.name: base

configs.description: Dual 400W DC supplies (PSU-401-DISB, screw-terminal input, intake airflow) with five FAN-402825-HD exhaust fans. The datasheet's DC input rating is -36 to -75 V at 16 A.
configs.name: dc

gaps.note: HIG section 10 tables the five front-panel lamps, the PSU and Fan FRU lamps and the out-of-band jack, and gives no table at all for the port lamps. The twenty-eight SFP arrows and the two QSFP28 lane strips therefore keep their components' off/on default rather than an invented link/activity vocabulary. Note that several rows elsewhere in those same tables are annotated as needing NOS integration to activate, so these may be NOS-defined rather than simply undocumented - which would be a different fix, and is why this is vendor-silent rather than nos-dependent.
gaps.wanted: a per-NOS LED table from UfiSpace or a NOS vendor, or photographs of a live unit with ports in known states

gaps.note: THIS IS A DEFECT IN A SHARED COMPONENT, NOT IN THIS DEVICE, and it is recorded here because this device is where the evidence turned up - specifically in the matched- scale comparison of the rendered rear against the rear photograph, which is the only check that could have found it. ufispace/fan-402825@1 places its status lamp at [2.0, 1.6] - top left of the face - and its own provenance cites 'HIG Fig 8 drawing' for the geometry. This device's HIG Figure 8 (fig-0014) and this device's rear photograph both put the lamp at the BOTTOM of the fan's right-hand flange, below a knurled thumbscrew and a red 'E' airflow tag that the component does not draw at all; the component also draws a plain round rotor where both images show a hex grille, and a straight handle bar where both show a curved tube. The two guides' Figure 8 is byte-for-byte the same image, so the component contradicts the figure it names. It was reused unchanged rather than forked or edited, because it is shared with the S9510-28DC and a correction would change that device's rendering on this device's reading.
gaps.wanted: a decision on ufispace/fan-402825's element positions and face art, or a photograph of the FRU out of the chassis

gaps.note: The S9510-28DC - the same 440 x 302 x 43.5 chassis, the same five FAN-402825, the same rear artwork - places its first fan bay at x 8.0 with a 53.2 mm pitch. Measured here from that artwork and from this device's rear photograph independently, fan 0's face starts at 18.0 and 18.2 respectively, on a 52.6 mm pitch, and both images draw a plain chassis border across 2.2-17.6 where the sibling puts fan metal. The bank's total span agrees (265.5 against 266.0); only its origin does not. This manifest carries the measured 18.1, and the sibling's 8.0 is either a different anchor or an error that should be checked before either is trusted.
gaps.wanted: a dimensioned rear drawing, or a tape on a real unit

gaps.note: The faceplate paints its first four SFP columns - ports 0 through 7 - in a blue band and the remaining six SFP+ columns in a plain dark one, while the datasheet lists all twenty as one thing, '20 x 100M/1/10G SFP+ ports'. Nothing in either document says what the blue marks. It could be a MACsec-capable subset, a 1G-capable subset, or housekeeping. The band is drawn because it is on the metal; no port carries an attribute derived from it.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace port-capability matrix, or a NOS port map for this platform

gaps.note: Neither held document states a maximum system power for this platform. The datasheet gives 'Typical power: 153.8 Watts (no transceiver)' and the input ratings, and the HIG's Connecting Power section gives provisioning instructions without a figure - unlike the same vendor's S9311-64D guide, which prints a maximum twice. power-max-w is therefore absent rather than estimated, and a reader budgeting a circuit has only the 400 W per-supply rating and the typical figure to work from.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace power calculator or a maximum-consumption line in a later guide revision

gaps.note: No held document prints an orderable chassis part number - the datasheet and the HIG name the product only as S9500-30XS, and the Available to Order block names only the two PSUs and one fan. The datasheet does say the platform has 'a standard SKU and a premium SKU', differing in memory and storage, without naming either. The S9510-28DC precedent applies: that model's -BN0B/-BR1B SKUs surfaced from the owner and from no held PDF, so orderable SKUs almost certainly exist. The configurations carry no part-numbers rather than invented ones.
gaps.wanted: a UfiSpace ordering guide, or the standard/premium SKU strings

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor

a top-level `profile:` naming the device class, so that `specified` has something to judge the attrs against - see spec/schemas/profiles.yaml for the classes that exist, which unlocks `specified` and with it the About panel, and comparison against other devices

provenance.attrs: datasheet - Specifications, Performance, Environmental, Regulatory Compliance and Accessories sections, transcribed into sections. Compliance strings kept verbatim, semicolon-separated, untidied; the NEBS line in particular is kept as the datasheet prints it. The datasheet's own typo in the timing block ('IEEE 1558v2' in the key features list, IEEE 1588v2 in the specification table) is not reproduced.
provenance.chassis: datasheet - 'Chassis (W x D x H) 1 RU, 440 x 302 x 43.5 mm', weight 4.76 kg without FRU; the HIG Component Physical Information table repeats the same triple and the same weight. 440 is the body and not a rack face: the HIG's accessory list ships 'Rack Mount Bracket ... 50.4 x 43 x 20mm (19' width rack)' as two separate parts, so the mounting hardware is additional to 440 and is not drawn here.
provenance.connector-sizes: std/rj45-ganged (12.7 x 11.0) is used for all four RJ45/RJ48 jacks rather than common/rj45-bezel@2 (17.0 x 14.9), which the S9510-28DC used for the same block and recorded a gap about because it 'slightly exceeds the drawn stack'. The reason is measured, not stylistic: the BITS/ToD apertures are drawn 12.26 mm wide on a 12.58 mm vertical pitch, and a 17 mm part cannot sit on that pitch at all. The same applies to the USB - the drawn aperture is 13.2 x 5.5, so std/usb-a (12.0 x 4.5) fits where common/usb-a@3 (17.0 x 9.3) does not.
provenance.fan-numbering: The rear panel numbers its fans 0-4, printed 'FAN <0' through 'FAN <4' at the top of each fan's right-hand flange in both the figure and the photograph. Those legends are NOT drawn, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: a fan-position number cannot live on an interchangeable FRU, so it would have to be chassis silkscreen - and there is no chassis metal to carry it, because the 42.2 mm fan face fills all but 1.3 mm of the 43.5 mm rear panel. Drawn as chassis silkscreen it would be painted under the fan modules and invisible. The numbering itself is certain and is what the bay ids and rel-pos carry.
provenance.led-semantics: HIG section 10 Front Panel LED table, transcribed rather than only cited. Five lamps - GNSS, SYNC, STAT, FAN, PWR - each with its own vocabulary, and three of them draw four distinct meanings out of two colours and two behaviours, which is why a state carries a behavior as well as a colour. The out-of-band jack is declared per element because its left lamp is green for 1G and its right amber for 10M/100M. The PSU FRU and Fan FRU tables belong to the modules and are already transcribed in their contracts. The guide gives NO table for the port lamps; see the port-led-semantics gap.
provenance.lifecycle: searched 2026-08-28: 'UfiSpace S9500-30XS end of life', and the vendor's own product page fetched and read for a notice. No announcement found; the product page is live and carries active downloads. none-announced is a real finding, not an absence.
provenance.port-arrows: drawing, and the figure is not self-consistent about ONE detail of it. Every column carries two small green arrows in the white band between its two apertures - one per port, up for the upper and down for the lower, the same idiom as the S9510-28DC. What the figure disagrees with itself about is their spread and order: the six right-hand columns draw a tight up-then-down pair at +/-2.1 mm about the column centre, legibly in that order at 14x; the eight left-hand columns draw them at +/-4.9 mm and, as far as much fainter marks can be read, down-then-up. Both cannot be the same faceplate. The right-hand block is the legible one and agrees with the sibling, so up-left/down-right at the sibling's +/-2.95 mm is used throughout, and the disagreement is recorded here rather than split.
provenance.port-numbers: drawing - the numbers ARE printed on the panel, on a painted band just outside each aperture, and they are drawn here. HIG fig-0015 prints each port's number twice: large, on the schematic module face, where a seated module would cover it, and small, on the coloured band above the top row and below the bottom row. The band is faceplate paint - the S9510-28DC records that as vendor-confirmed for the same family - so the small number is the one the metal carries. Even numbers on the top row and odd on the bottom, left to right, 0-27 across the SFP columns and a separate 0-1 for the two QSFP28.
provenance.power: datasheet 'Typical power: 153.8 Watts (no transceiver)' - the vendor's own scope, so power-envelope is bare. No maximum is published for this platform in either held document: the HIG's Connecting Power section gives provisioning instructions and an input rating and never a system maximum, unlike the S9311-64D's, so power-max-w is absent rather than guessed. The PSU rating is 400 W per supply from the ordering lines. These are the vendor's figures as the vendor states them and are NOT reconciled against the module set; the fans publish no draw at all, so any total built from the modelled modules is a floor.
provenance.psus: drawing - the two supplies are on the FRONT of this chassis, at the left of the faceplate, which is what makes it a front-service telco box. PSU1's metal face measures x 64.96-115.70 (50.74 mm against the stated 50.5) and y 1.6-41.8 (40.2); PSU0 sits one pitch left at 6.22, so the bay pitch is 58.74 mm. That pitch was derived here from this figure alone and lands within 0.1% of the 58.7 the S9510-28DC carries - the same chassis, the same PSU-401, measured by somebody else from a different document - which is corroboration rather than a copied number. The blue release latch is drawn OUTSIDE the face to its left, in the gutter that carries the vertical PSU0/PSU1 legend; ufispace/psu-401-dc draws its latch inside its own 50.5 width, and that difference is the component's business, not the bay's.
provenance.rear-layout: drawing/photo - five fan bays across the left and a hex vent field filling the right. HIG fig-0014's rear elevation and the rear photograph are the same artwork at different scales and agree on the one number that anchors everything: fan 0's face starts at x 18.1 mm (18.0 from the figure at 3.182 px/mm, 18.2 from the photograph at 3.782 px/mm). The pitch is 52.6 mm, the mean of three repeated features measured in both images - the airflow tag, the status lamp and the thumbscrew - which individually give 52.25 to 53.43 because both images carry slight perspective (the handles' bounding boxes shrink measurably from left to right). The vent field runs from 285.8 to 435.2. NOTE THIS DISAGREES WITH THE S9510-28DC, which places the same five fans on the same chassis starting at x 8.0: both images here put the first fan ten millimetres further right, and the light chassis border they both draw between 2.2 and 17.6 mm is where that model puts fan metal.
provenance.scale-gate: THE FRONT FIGURE FAILS A NAIVE ASPECT GATE AND IS STILL USABLE, and the reason is worth writing down because it decides every number on this face. The HIG's port overview (fig-0015) measures 1436 x 150 px body against a stated 440 x 43.5 mm chassis: aspect 9.57 against a true 10.115, 5.7% out. So does the front photograph, independently, at 9.49. Two images agreeing with each other and disagreeing with the spec table is not two bad drawings; it is both of them drawing something the spec table does not measure. What they draw is the chassis's top and bottom lips as well as its front face - the strip is taller than the faceplate. The axes were therefore calibrated separately, each against an object whose real size the vendor states, and each confirmed twice: X - the panel width 1436 px = 440 mm gives 3.2636 px/mm. On that scale the SFP column pitch measures 14.32 mm against the 14.25 mm std/sfp-ganged standard, and PSU1's metal face measures 50.8 mm against the HIG component table's 50.5. Neither of those numbers set the scale, and both land on it. Y - the PSU face is the only object on this face whose height the vendor states (40.2 mm). It measures 131 px, so 3.259 px/mm - within 0.1% of the X scale, which is what an orthographic drawing should be, and which the panel-height reading (3.448) is not. Vertical positions are therefore y = 1.6 + (py - 11) / 3.259, anchoring the PSU face's top edge at 1.6 mm; that puts its bottom edge at 41.8 in a 43.5 chassis, a symmetric 1.6/1.7 mm margin, which is the check that the anchor is right. Both scales are carried as `drawing` confidence and are good to about 0.3 mm.
provenance.sfp-layout: drawing - fourteen columns of two, in two runs with ONE chassis web between them: eight columns then the web at x 319.6, then six more. Column centres are 210.35 + 14.32k for k=0..7 and 328.47 + 14.32k for k=0..5, taken from the twenty-eight green port arrows in the band between the rows (28 blobs, one pair per column, pair centres regressing on a 14.32 mm pitch with no residual over 0.8 mm) and cross-checked against the bright column separators. Rows: std/sfp-ganged tops at 8.83 and 26.48, each centred on the drawn module face (the figure draws SEATED modules, whose faces measure 8.9 and 9.2 mm tall inside a 10.4 mm cage opening - a module is smaller than its cage, which is why the face is not the aperture). Ports 0-19 are the SFP+ run and 20-27 the SFP28 run, per the datasheet's counts and the yellow band, which starts exactly at column 11's left edge.
provenance.side-faces: estimated. No held figure dimensions either side wall. The HIG's rack-mounting section fixes the chassis to the posts through the two 50.4 x 43 mm brackets and says nothing about side features, and the grounding section puts the lug on the RIGHT side wall (HIG Figures 19-22 and the fig-0011 inset, which magnifies a two-hole lug on the chassis's right rear corner). Both side faces therefore carry only the bracket screws and, on the right, the grounding lug - positions estimated, and LEFT has x = 0 at the REAR while RIGHT has x = 0 at the FRONT, stated here because both faces carry only symmetric content and nothing else would expose the convention.
provenance.sources: UfiSpace S9500-30XS datasheet (working/intake/ufispace/converted/s9500-30xs-datasheet) for dimensions, weight, port inventory, platform, timing, power, environment, compliance and the FRU ordering lines; S9500-30XS Hardware Installation Guide (s9500-30xs-hig) for the faceplate and rear figures, the FRU dimension table, the LED tables and grounding; three vendor product renders (photos/s9500-30xs-1-angle, -2-front, -3-rear) for colour, counts and confirmation. Checked for a vendor 3D model before trusting any figure, per the skill: the intake stages GLBs for ReadyLinks only, and the S9500-30XS product page embeds no model-viewer and offers no .glb/.gltf/.usdz or CAD download - so this model rests on figures and the gates below apply in full.
provenance.timing-block: drawing - five SMA jacks in two rows, read off HIG fig-0015 at 8x: 1PPS IN and OUT on the upper row at x 140.18 and 155.05, y 16.64; GNSS ANT, 10MHZ IN and 10MHZ OUT on the lower row at x 124.83, 139.60 and 155.05, y 31.98. The IN and OUT columns line up between the two rows, which is the check that the five centres are read right. The datasheet calls all five SMA ('1 x GNSS input SMA, 1 x 1PPS input/output SMA, 1 x 10MHz input/output SMA'). All five are ROUND: common/sma-jack was not used, even though it is the library's panel SMA part and the S9510-28DC uses it for the same job, because it draws a HEX nut and both the figure at 8x and the front photograph show a circular knurled ring here. Each jack is therefore std/sma - the 6.35 mm registry bore, round - on a gold decor disc for the nut, the same construction the S9311-64D uses for its round SMB jacks. The disc sizes carry a real difference in the artwork rather than averaging it away: the figure draws the 1PPS pair 9.6 mm across the nut and the other three only 7.1, a 35% difference well above what this figure resolves. Then BITS over ToD in their own silver frame (RJ48 over RJ45, an 12.58 mm stack pitch), then the out-of-band RJ45, the USB-A and the console RJ45 in a third frame.
provenance.top-face: drawing, and this is the one figure that passes the aspect gate outright. HIG fig-0011's footprint drawing measures 901 x 618 px against 440 x 302 mm - aspect 1.458 against a true 1.457, 0.07% out - so it is orthographic and carries absolute geometry at 2.047 px/mm on both axes. y = 0 is the REAR, per the house convention and the drawing itself, which puts the fan handles at the top edge and the front bezel at the bottom. Two full-width stadium recesses at y 45.9 and 187.2, four short ones in two pairs at y 109.0 and 271.2, and two rows of lid screws at y 6.8 and 85.0 on a 52.8 mm pitch that matches the fan pitch below them.
